query: For a CoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy matrix evaluated in sliding from room temperature to 800 °C, what single intervention could overcome the difficulty of maintaining low coefficient of friction and wear rate throughout the full temperature range? Earlier studies of other self-lubricating material systems reported low coefficients of friction at 704 °C and favorable friction and wear behavior over broad temperature ranges. However, these results do not resolve the limited understanding of wide-temperature tribological performance in CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloys, and effectiveness must be maintained as operating temperature, load, and environment vary. Formulate one hypothesis that identifies a single intervention without presupposing its class, explains its mechanism, predicts friction and wear relative to the starting CoCrFeNi material, defines its temperature, load, and environmental boundaries, relates it to prior evidence, and specifies a controlled experiment with a clear result that would falsify the hypothesis.

AbstractThe effect and mechanism of grain sizes on the tribological behavior of CoCrFeMnNi high entropy alloy (HEA) were studied by friction experiments and wear morphology analysis. Under normal low load and low sliding speed, the primary wear mechanism of the HEA samples is adhesive wear. With the increase in sliding speed, the wear mechanisms of the samples are adhesive wear and oxidation wear. The oxide layer formed under the action of friction heat of the coarse grain (CG) sample is easy to break due to the softening of the CG. With the increase of normal load and sliding speed, the wear mechanisms of the HEA samples are mainly adhesive wear, oxidation wear, and plastic deformation. The oxide layer of CG sample has many cracks, and the worn surface also has plastic deformation, which leads to the increase of friction coefficient and specific wear rate and the decrease of wear resistance. Therefore, the fine grain size HEA sample has better wear resistance than the CG sample due to its high surface strength.Keywords: high entropy alloy, grain size, tribological behavior, wear mechanism

In the present study, the tribological properties of different grain sizes CoCrFeMnNi HEAs were systematically analyzed based on sliding experiments and worn surface morphology characterization under different sliding speeds and normal loads. The results can be summarized as follows: Under the normal low load and low sliding speed, the main wear mechanism of FG and CG samples is adhesive wear. With the increase in sliding speed, the wear mechanisms are adhesive wear and oxidation wear. However, the material of CG is easy to soften under the action of friction heat during high sliding speed, and the oxide layer formed is easy to fracture. Under the normal high load, the wear mechanisms of FG and CG samples are mainly adhesive wear, oxidation wear, and plastic deformation with the increase of sliding speed. The oxidation layer formed on CG sample has many cracks, and the wear surface of CG sample also has plastic deformation, resulting in an increase in friction coefficient and specific wear rate and a decrease in wear resistance. Therefore, under high load and low load, FG sample has good wear resistance due to its high surface strength.

decision.trend: Research has been focused on improving the tribological properties of high-entropy alloys (HEAs) through various methods such as grain size control, alloying additions, and surface modification. Studies have shown that fine-grained HEAs exhibit better wear resistance than coarse-grained ones. Additionally, the introduction of certain elements such as W and SiC can enhance the wear resistance of HEAs. Recent studies have also explored the use of 2D HEA nanoflakes as solid lubricants, which have shown promising results.
decision.unsolved: Despite the progress made in improving the tribological properties of HEAs, there is still a lack of understanding of the underlying mechanisms and the effects of various parameters such as temperature, load, and environment on the wear behavior of HEAs. Furthermore, the development of HEAs with consistent and reliable tribological properties across a wide range of temperatures and conditions remains a challenge.
decision.lever: investigating the role of grain size and lattice distortion on the tribological behavior of CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloys using advanced characterization techniques such as TEM and XRD
decision.why: This next step is proposed because understanding the relationship between grain size, lattice distortion, and tribological behavior is crucial for developing HEAs with consistent and reliable tribological properties. Advanced characterization techniques such as TEM and XRD can provide valuable insights into the microstructural evolution and deformation mechanisms of HEAs during wear, which can inform the design of new HEAs with improved tribological properties.
